newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan mulls purchase of 408,500T corn/soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan mulls purchase of 408,500T corn/soybeans.

text.p: Taiwanese grain and oilseeds buyers have shown strong interest in possibly buying up to 272,500 tonnes of soybeans and 136,000 tonnes of corn, local traders said on Monday.
The importers want to lock in supplies at current levels ahead of an anticipated increase in world prices, they said.
"Soybean futures are quite bullish right now," a buyer at Formosa Oilseed Processing Corp said.
Soybeans could test US$8.00 per bushel in the near term, the buyer added. Other buyers said they expected to see a rally push prices to between $7.60 to $7.80 a bushel.
The price of the March soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (COBT) closed unchanged on Friday at $7.48 a bushel.
"Soybean has remained strong since the latest bullish USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) crop estimates issued on Friday, January 10," a buyer said.
Taiwanese corn buyers also plan to return to the market to secure supplies to cover their commercial requirements.
One buyer from Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group said the group hoped that the apparent return of an unpredictable China to the international corn market would push prices lower.
Taiwan's Hui Shung Group and CK Group will retender for a combined corn and soybeans shipment that they had passed on earlier in January, traders said.

The Taichung and Kaoshung divisions of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association may also place tenders for up to 216,000 tonnes of soybeans, they added. Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender on Tuesday for a combined shipment of 30,000 tonnes of soybeans and corn and on the same day Members Feed Industry Group will tender for a 54,000-tonne corn shipment.
Local soymeal prices for Taipei delivery were quoted on Monday at between T$9.45-$9.65 a kg, up from T$9.40-$9.60 a kg last week.
Corn powder was indicated at $8.20 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from the previous week's $6.75 a kg.
Domestic flour prices on Monday ranged between $14.55 to $15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.

Bulk grain freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan were quoted at about US$13.50 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico between $23.50 and $24.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
